evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function CARD8 mutation causes NLRP3 inflammasome activation and Crohn's disease.
evidence.snippet: Whole exome sequencing and PCR studies identified the affected individuals as having a V44I mutation in a single allele of the T60 isoform of CARD8.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion. A heterozygous V44I substitution in the T60 isoform of CARD8 abolishes its binding to NLRP3. The variant protein still oligomerizes with normal T60 and T48 CARD8, and these mixed oligomers cannot bind NLRP3, so a single mutant allele lowers total CARD8 inhibitory function.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function CARD8 mutation causes NLRP3 inflammasome activation and Crohn's disease.

evidence.snippet: the CARD8 mutation provides more definite proof that increased and excessive IL-1β is capable of causing Crohn's disease because in this case the NLRP3 abnormality is not coupled with another abnormality

nodes.description: In resting cells CARD8 binds NLRP3 and prevents its activation by weak stimuli. Without functional CARD8, NLRP3 oligomerizes more readily after NLRP3 activators. Intact CARD8 also keeps NLRP3 ubiquitinated and serine-phosphorylated, two modifications that hold NLRP3 inactive; the mutant does not.
